restoration_note: The teaching describes the cosmic mechanism of light's extraction from the threefold strongholds: rays of Divine Truth penetrate firmament-by-firmament through great gates open across the four climes, drawing captive light by the hand together with the small Pillar, sorting one kind upward to the Living Ones and consigning the other to the lower side. Most editor restorations confirmed: single-letter completions (ⲗ in ⲁⲗⲗⲁ, ⲕ in ⲕⲁⲧⲁ, ⲟ in ⲟⲩⲉⲛ, articles), Greek loanwords (ⲡⲩⲗⲏ, ⲕⲗⲓⲙⲁ, ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ), and structural formulae (ⲡⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ, ⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ). One editor reading corrected: {13} ⲛⲓⲥⲃⲏⲩⲉ is better read as 'walls' (Sahidic plural of ⲥⲟⲃⲧ) rather than 'firmaments,' since ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ appears as the distinct technical term in the very next line. {7} restored as ⲡⲣⲓⲉ (Radiance from the lexicon) — the masculine subject that 'goes upward and becomes the light of the rays.' Several short lacunae at line edges ({2}, {3}, {4}, {5}, {8}, {11}, {29}, {32}) lack sufficient parallel or trace and are left unrestored. The structural argument is firm even where agent-names are obscured.

restorations.basis: Editor restoration confirmed: completes ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'of light' with surviving ⲁⲓⲛⲉ; parallel to ⲡⲓⲗⲁⲟⲩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲱⲛⲍ̄ ⲍⲓ ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ in next line.
Editor restoration confirmed: directly parallel to ⲡⲓϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲟⲣⲉ in surrounding context; visible ⲙ at line end fits ⲙ[ⲡⲓϣⲁⲙⲧ].
16-char lacuna at end of clause 'strongholds which surround the cosmos'; could be a transitional formula ('show us...', 'whole...'), but no trace and no parallel constrains the fill.
2-char interior gap in ⲙ̄ⲙⲁ..ⲛ; editor notes possibility of ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ + suffix or unidentified compound. Could be ⲙⲁⲉⲓⲛ 'sign' but English 'the[___] of this kind of life' is too ambiguous to fix.
14-char lacuna at line end after 'this kind of life that comes upward'; no trace and no determinative parallel.
4-char gap at clause start before ⲁⲗⲗⲁ 'but'; could end preceding sentence, but partial ('. .') is too weak to constrain.
Single letter completing ⲁⲗⲗⲁ 'but' from surviving ⲁⲗ_ⲁ.

4-char masculine subject that 'goes upward and becomes the light of the rays.' ⲡⲡⲣⲓⲉ (Radiance, lexicon) — same root as ⲡⲣⲏ 'sun'/'shining' — fits both length and the spiritual arc of light ascending.
2-char gap with single trace at end of ϣⲱⲡⲉ '(it) becomes'; could be a short particle or beginning of next noun; no determining parallel.
2-char gap directly before ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'light'; the demonstrative-article ⲡⲓ fits length and parallels Lycopolitan use of ⲡⲓ- with abstract masculine nouns. Alternative: short particle.
4-char relative-clause verb modifying ⲛⲁⲕⲧⲓⲛ 'rays.' ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine/radiate' (lexicon, same root as Radiance) parallels 'gates of shining-forth' (ⲛⲣⲱⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ϩⲡⲡⲓⲉ) two lines below.
2-char gap with only ⲛ visible after 'channel of'; could be ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ (too long), ⲛⲣⲏ, or other; no determining trace.
Editor single-letter restoration confirmed: probably the relative ⲉ- or circumstantial prefix before ⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ.

Correcting editor: ⲛⲓⲥⲃⲏⲩⲉ = plural of ⲥⲟⲃⲧ/ⲥⲁⲃⲧ̄ 'wall' (lexicon: 'the protecting boundary of the cosmos'). The next clause uses ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ separately as the 'firmament' technical term, so this slot must be the cognate but distinct cosmic boundary.
Editor single-letter restoration confirmed: completes ⲕⲁⲧⲁ (Greek κατά) 'according to'.
Editor restoration confirmed: ϩⲧⲟⲉ 'four' demands a noun; 'gates' (πύλη) recurs throughout the passage as the central cosmic-architectural term.
Editor single-letter restoration confirmed: completes ⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'open' (qualitative).
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲕⲗⲓⲙⲁ 'climes' (Greek κλίμα) with ⲉⲩ- relative-clause prefix continuing on the next line; the four climes are the structural frame of the whole teaching.
Editor single-letter restoration confirmed: completes ⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'open' (qualitative), parallel to line 12.
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲕⲧⲓⲛ 'the light of the rays' continues as subject of ⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ in next line.
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲛ̄ⲛ̄ⲁⲕⲧⲓⲛ 'of the rays' — genitive marker plus plural article completing the formula 'light of the rays.'
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲙ̄ⲙⲁ ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ 'in that very place' is the standard Lycopolitan formula and is completed across line 15.
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ 'that very (place)' standard Lycopolitan deictic completing the phrase from previous line.
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲡⲕⲟⲩⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲧⲩⲗⲟⲥ 'the small Pillar' — Manichaean cosmological figure linked to the Pillar of Glory (lexicon: path of ascent).
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲉⲧϣⲟⲟⲡ 'which exists/is' standard Lycopolitan relative formula; matches surviving ⲟⲟⲡ.
Editor single-letter restoration confirmed: completes ⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ 'that very (place).'
Editor restoration of ϣⲁⲩⲙⲟⲩϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'they are filled forth'; fits the spiritual arc of rays gathering captive light at that very place. Sense plausible but verb identification uncertain.
Editor restoration confirmed: directional ⲁⲛ̄- before ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ 'firmament,' fitting the formula 'firmament by firmament' of the ascent.
5-char gap completing 'they are made firm in the firmaments [all]'; ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ fits length and matches the cosmological universality the teaching emphasizes ('every cosmos,' 'the four climes').
2-char gap before conjunctive ⲛ̄ⲥⲉ-; could be ⲁⲩⲱ or end of preceding word; no determining trace.
Editor restoration confirmed: ⲡⲥⲁⲛⲧⲡⲉ ⲧⲏⲣⲥ̄ 'the whole upper place' + ⲍⲁ 'under' beginning the sorting clause; the 'upper place' = the Living Ones above, where chosen kind is borne.
Editor single-letter restoration confirmed: completes ⲧⲛ̄ article before ⲛⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ 'the Living Ones.'
4-char gap between ⲍⲱⲱϩ 'also' and ϣⲁⲩ-; likely a verb relating to the rejected kind, but the doubled verbal structure with {33} ϣⲁⲩⲛⲁⲝⲥ̄ does not constrain this slot.
Editor restoration confirmed: ϣⲁⲩⲛⲁⲝⲥ̄ 'they habitually cast her' — the rejected kind sent down to the lower side, parallel to the chosen kind borne up to the Living Ones.
Editor single-letter restoration confirmed: article ⲡ̄- before ⲥⲁⲙ̄ⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'lower side.'
